elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Article II.iii as rendered grants the licence "to Licensee and, upon written notice to Licensor, its Affiliates", and the conflicting restrictions in (b) and (e) are conformed to carve out "Licensee's Affiliates licensed hereunder". "AFFILIATE" is a defined term (s.1.1), so the grant is operative.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No contractor language was added; restriction (e) as rendered still limits use/access to "employees of the Licensee or its Affiliates licensed hereunder", and (b) still bars third-party use except Affiliates. To meet this element the drafter must add "and contractors acting on Licensee's behalf" to the grant and to both carve-outs in (b) and (e).

Nothing in the rendered grant or in Article IV (36-month term) states that any paid-up licence is perpetual; the grant remains conditioned on "Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement". No perpetuity language was inserted.
The grant is silent on irrevocability and remains "subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement" and conditioned on continued payment; no "irrevocable" wording was added.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No edit was made to the termination provisions to confine termination of the licence to uncured material breach; the finding expressly disclaims pursuing this item.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Rewritten Article XX(a) provides the licence "shall continue in full force and effect and may be transferred, without Licensor's consent, to Licensee's successor in such merger, acquisition or other Change of Control", and s.13.4(c) still routes any Change of Control to that section, so the consent bar does not re-attach.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Grant now reads "grants to Licensee and, upon written notice to Licensor, its Affiliates"; the two otherwise contradictory prohibitions (third-party use in (b); non-employee individuals in (e)) are conformed so the Affiliate grant is not defeated by retained language.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Article XX(a) as rendered replaces automatic termination with continuation plus transfer "without Licensor's consent, to Licensee's successor in such merger, acquisition or other Change of Control"; the Change of Control definition survives and the assignment clause cross-reference remains intact.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: both the affiliate-on-written-notice element and the M&A successor transfer element are met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment.
Preferred level is incomplete: contractor coverage, perpetual and irrevocable paid-up rights, and termination only for uncured material breach were not attempted.

Minimality holds. "Licensee" is a single named entity (551 FX IB Associates, LLC) and does not include Affiliates, so the affiliate grant is not duplicative. The edits to (b) and (e) are not gratuitous personnel edits: the retained words "any third party" and "any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee" expressly contradict the new Affiliate grant, so conforming them is necessary. Deleting the Change of Control consent and deemed-unreasonable-withholding sentences is consequential to removing the automatic termination that blocked transfer; leaving them would create a dangling consent mechanic.
No broad "notwithstanding" override of the assignment clause was used; the transfer permission is stated directly as "without Licensor's consent", which is the least intrusive route.

Intent preserved: no new Vendor-side assignment exception was created, the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition and the s.13.4(c) cross-reference to it remain operative, and the Field of Use, payment condition and non-exclusive character of the grant are untouched. The Article XX heading ("Certain Other Events of Termination") still governs the remaining subsections, so retaining it is not a contradiction.

If the drafter wants to reach the preferred level, the repairs are: add "and contractors acting on its behalf" to the grant and to the carve-outs in (b) and (e); state that licences for which all fees have been paid are perpetual and irrevocable; and limit termination of the licence during the term to uncured material breach.
